records.title: Variability of responses and complications in hypobaric hypoxia
records.locator: Abstract 219, printed p. 421, PDF p. 37, Methods and Results
records.note: Reports 30 participants, four sessions at 46.5 kPa and two asystole cases. The same combination in Westendorp et al. Study A indicates likely overlap. Use the later paper for structured outcome counts.

records.title: Hypoxic syncope
records.locator: Protocol A and B, Studies A and B, pp. 411–412, Figs. 1–4
records.note: Two crossover protocols with different primary questions. Clinical endpoints in this extraction are hypoxic cardiovascular reactions. DCS was discussed as a separate diagnosis, with no DCS surveillance numerator reported for either protocol.

observations.locator: Protocol A and Study A, p. 411
observations.note: The source records six exposures with lightheadedness, pallor, sweating and bradycardia in five volunteers. Two affected people had asystole. This is a hypoxic adverse-event endpoint.
Two distinct participants each had syncope and documented asystole. The source gives durations of 13 and 18 seconds. Both episodes fall within the six symptomatic exposures.

observations.locator: Protocol B, p. 411, and Study B, p. 412
observations.note: Three episodes occurred while seated and two upon standing. The full text distinguishes one documented loss of consciousness from the combined syncope or near-syncope endpoint.

observations.locator: Protocol B, p. 411, and Study B, p. 412
observations.note: No adverse reaction was reported during hypoxic exposure without ANP. These five people took part in both conditions.

records.title: Atrial natriuretic peptide improves pulmonary gas exchange in subjects exposed to hypoxia
records.locator: Author abstract, Methods and Results, PMID 8393637
records.note: Westendorp 1997 identifies this as the main study after describing its five-person pilot. The main paper reports 11 healthy mountaineers and 5 ng/kg/min ANP versus 10 ng/kg/min in the pilot. Participant overlap and syncope ascertainment in the main study are unreported.

records.title: Prolonged asystole during hypobaric chamber training
records.locator: Case Report pp. 520–521, Fig. 1, and official erratum p. 619
records.note: Selected case with 16 seconds of asystole during chamber training. The erratum changes the recovery statement to spontaneous recovery without CPR or intervention. The case narrative describes mask replacement and positioning. The two statements are retained and treatment attribution remains unclear.

observations.locator: Case Report, p. 520, Fig. 1, and erratum p. 619
observations.note: One published case with 16 seconds of monitored asystole. The training denominator is unavailable. The official correction changes the recovery description.

records.title: Acute hypoxia in a simulated high-altitude airdrop scenario due to oxygen system failure
records.locator: Methods, Participants and Exposure, and Results, first paragraph
records.note: One of nine volunteers lost consciousness with documented profound desaturation. The authors interpret this as hypoxic syncope. Preserve the simulated peak altitude separately from the altitude of syncope.

observations.note: Source places loss of consciousness at 25,400 ft and reports profound desaturation. Eight volunteers completed the full profile. The paper discusses DCS risk separately and gives no adjudicated DCS tally.
